facts.text: GCMS Organic Analysis Oven was deployed at Utopia Planitia during Viking 2 in 1976.

Surface funnel and motorized soil distribution sieve that transported regolith samples into miniature pyrolysis ovens. The ovens pyrolyzed soil at 50°C, 200°C, 350°C, and 500°C to volatilize compounds for mass spectrometer analysis.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Detected trace water and carbon dioxide liberated by heating, but found no organic compounds above parts-per-billion levels due to highly reactive soil oxidizers.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Utopia Planitia.
Its puzzling negative results spurred decades of research into perchlorates and Martian soil oxidizers, eventually solved by Phoenix and Curiosity.
